## Linux clients

The chart can now run the Helmut4 Linux client (`mcp_hc`) as an optional component. Several
**types** side by side, each its own Deployment with its own mount points, sizing and pool of
render-node users — and each independently autoscalable.

The obstacle to running it as a Deployment is identity: a client authenticates from a
`helmut.auto.login` file generated by hand for one machine, so every replica would present the
same user. Each pod now runs an initContainer that claims a *free* render-node user from its
type's pool and generates that user's autologin file on startup. Replicas become
interchangeable, and scaling is bounded only by how many users and licence seats exist.

```yaml
linuxClients:
  enabled: true
  adminCredentials:
    existingSecret: "helmut-client-admin"
  types:
    render:
      userPrefix: "linux-render-"      # claims linux-render-01 … -08
      appMounts: true
      autoscaling:
        enabled: true
        maxReplicas: 8
```

Off by default; existing installations are unaffected.

- Endpoints come from the `service-config` ConfigMap, so clients talk to the services directly
  and never traverse the ingress — nothing to configure, nothing to keep in sync.
- Mounts are additive: `appMounts` reuses the shares the microservices get, `volumes` adds any
  other PVC.
- Rollouts use `maxSurge: 0`, so an upgrade never needs more users than replicas.
- `maxReplicas` is bounded twice — by the user pool *and* by free concurrent-client licence
  seats. Both failure modes are documented.

The initContainer image is built from [`client-autologin/`](https://github.com/moovit-sp-gmbh/helmut4-helm-chart/tree/main/client-autologin) in this
repo and published to `ghcr.io/moovit-sp-gmbh/helmut4-client-autologin`.

### Scaling down does not lose work

Scale-down, `kubectl drain` and rollouts all delete pods, and nothing tells the client that a
render is about to be cut short. Every client pod therefore carries a `preStop` hook that holds
SIGTERM while the container is still working. On by default.

```yaml
linuxClients:
  gracefulShutdown:
    enabled: true
    cpuThresholdMillicores: 200   # below this the client counts as idle
    pollSeconds: 10
    maxWaitSeconds: 3600          # hard cap, so a wedged client can't block a drain
```

Two details that matter more than they look:

- **CPU is read from the container's own cgroup**, not from `top` or `/proc`. Both of those
  report the *node's* load rather than the pod's, and the client image is Alpine — busybox `top`
  has no `Cpu(s)` line, so the usual `top -bn1 | grep "Cpu(s)"` recipe produces a nonsense
  number in it and the hook would never release early.
- **`terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is derived**, not configured: it is raised to
  `maxWaitSeconds + 30` whenever it would otherwise be smaller. A grace period shorter than the
  drain means the kubelet SIGKILLs the pod mid-job and the hook accomplishes nothing — so that
  combination is now impossible to configure.

The trade-off is deliberate: a pod can sit in `Terminating` for as long as its current job. That
makes draining a busy node slow, and with `maxSurge: 0` a rollout of N replicas serialises to
N × job length. Roll out when the fleet is quiet, or set `gracefulShutdown.enabled: false`.

Setup guide: [docs/LINUX-CLIENTS.md](https://github.com/moovit-sp-gmbh/helmut4-helm-chart/blob/main/docs/LINUX-CLIENTS.md)
